newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates edge down, DTCs set lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates edge down, DTCs set lower.

text.p: Dutch deposits moved slightly lower on Monday, while overnight rates lost some six basis points in slow trade.
Dealers said the drop in call was not due to fundamentals.
"It's no more than a correction on Friday's rise, when overnight money was pushed up by a couple of big buyers who wanted to settle their business, thus pushing it higher," one dealer said.
Call money was quoted between 3.00 and 3.06 percent bid, changing hands around 3.0625 and 3.125 percent, down from 3.18 percent before the week-end.
One-month to one-year deposits were all quoted two basis points lower than on Friday, without a clear reason.
"Maybe money market rates rose a little bit too much last week in a belated reaction to the rate hike, so now they're easing back somewhat," one dealer suggested.
Another added such a minor move in an empty market did not mean much.

Dealers said the Finance Ministry's Agent had lowered prices on Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) by some two or three basis points during the morning, which contributed to the slight drop in money market rates.
In the afternoon, the April DTC programme was set at 3.06 percent, the May programme at 3.08 percent and the December programme at 3.22 percent, dealers said.
DTCs are short-term securities issued by the Dutch government on a discount-to-face-value basis.
The guilder lost some ground against the mark, trading at 112.53 per 100 marks, versus 112.50 on Friday afternoon, but dealers said this hardly affected the market.
